vectors.name: document-model/input-size/json-at-declared-maximum-succeeds
vectors.comment: D-23 boundary pair, accepted half. The input is `{"a":"` (6 bytes), 12 `x` and `"}` (2 bytes): 20 bytes, exactly the declared maximum of 20, which MUST be accepted (equal is accepted). declared_max_input_bytes is vector-local; an implementation with no configuration surface for it reports skip.

vectors.name: document-model/input-size/json-one-byte-over-declared-maximum-fails
vectors.comment: D-23 boundary pair, rejected half: the same input with 13 `x`, 21 bytes against a declared maximum of 20. The path is `$` (E-11), and the size is checked before any parsing, so the input's validity is not a factor.

vectors.name: document-model/input-size/yaml-at-declared-maximum-succeeds
vectors.comment: D-23 boundary pair, accepted half, YAML. `a: ` (3 bytes), 16 `x` and a newline: 20 bytes, exactly the declared maximum of 20, accepted. D-23 applies to every format, plain alias-free YAML included (D-22 does not).

vectors.name: document-model/input-size/yaml-one-byte-over-declared-maximum-fails
vectors.comment: D-23 boundary pair, rejected half, YAML: 17 `x`, 21 bytes against 20. Rejected with `document.limit.input-size` at `$`, although the input contains no alias and so is exempt from D-22.

vectors.name: document-model/input-size/multibyte-at-declared-maximum-succeeds
vectors.comment: D-23 counts bytes. `é` is two bytes in UTF-8. `{"a":"` (6), six of them (12) and `"}` (2) is 20 bytes and 14 characters; the declared maximum is 20, so it is accepted.

vectors.name: document-model/input-size/multibyte-counts-bytes-not-characters-fails
vectors.comment: D-23 counts bytes, not characters. Seven `é` give 22 bytes but only 15 characters. Against a declared maximum of 20 the input is rejected, which a character count (15 <= 20) would not do. This vector separates the two.
